scope: Bibliographic/analysis metadata from prior scientific dossiers; full text and verbatim excerpts omitted; historic read levels not re-performed by packaging

sources.authors: T. N. T. Goodman and S. L. Lee
sources.title: Another extremal property of perfect splines
sources.journal: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 70(2), 129–135 (1978)
sources.provenance: Original article text, uploaded by author Tim N. T. Goodman; publisher direct PDF was inaccessible through the research tool
sources.reduction: k=2, 2M+2 Hermite data yields n=2M; Theorem 1 if rho exceeds minimum derivative norm, Corollary 6 at equality. Clamped k=n=2 special case yields A Delta²/16, hence rho Delta²/8 for a difference bounded by 2rho.
sources.obstruction: No additional first-derivative speed-band constraint is imposed by this theorem. No objective-value lower is supplied.

sources.authors: T. Scarinci and V. M. Veliov
sources.title: Higher-order numerical scheme for linear quadratic problems with bang–bang controls
sources.reduction: Take normalized input u=-a with alpha=-A0/Delta, beta=-A1/Delta²; their interval length and midpoint become the candidate negative interval exactly.
sources.obstruction: Theorem 3.1 is a conditional optimizer/discretization convergence result and is not itself a theorem about arbitrary nonlinear workload values. Moment reconstruction is usable independently of those extra assumptions.

sources.authors: R. A. DeVore, R. Howard and C. Micchelli
sources.title: Optimal nonlinear approximation
sources.provenance: Original primary article scan on a third-party host; authorship and publication independently verified through author institution
sources.reduction: Supplies classical second-order Sobolev approximation scale, not the physical workload value-gap claim.
sources.obstruction: Continuous encoding requirement; norm error versus maximized scalar value; fixed nonlinear representation class versus infimum over encoders. Even unrestricted linear-functional gaps measure distance to closed convex hull, not distance to the representation set.

sources.authors: J. M. Aldaz, O. Kounchev and H. Render
sources.title: Bernstein operators for exponential polynomials
sources.provenance: Author primary preprint; journal metadata cross-checked in author institution repository
sources.reduction: For switching S''=q and P(D)q=0, S lies in ker D²P(D). Dimension d=D_q+2 and maximum imaginary frequency Omega yield at most (d−1)(floor(T Omega/pi)+1) zeros by partitioning into short intervals. L1 best-affine duality produces exact feasible sign(S) optimizer for the central endpoint moments.
sources.obstruction: Finite dictionary must be fixed in physical time. Nonlinear e(theta(t)) or active-band multiplier terms need not remain in that space. Global dimension-minus-one zero counting fails on long oscillatory intervals.

sources.title: On Bang-Bang Constrained Solutions of a Control System
sources.journal: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization 33(2), 554–567 (1995)
sources.reduction: Direct ordered upper/lower bang envelopes for the double-integrator specialization with fixed endpoint position and velocity.
sources.obstruction: Not a lower bound on all scalar objective approximations. This pass does not assert complete K+2 subsumption for all sign-changing nonlinear objectives.

sources.authors: M. Caponigro, R. Ghezzi, B. Piccoli and E. Trélat
sources.title: Regularization of chattering phenomena via bounded variation controls
sources.reduction: Precedent for quantitative value-versus-variation regularization; not a direct matching lower for the fixed workload family.
sources.obstruction: Additional controllability/regularity hypotheses and regularization/convergence quantifiers differ from a workload-indexed m-jump value lower.
